title: Molletes
skill: Using the oven with mitts on

notes.text: Use two sheet pans, one on each rack, and swap them halfway through the second bake.

move.title: In and out of a hot oven
move.body: Molletes are a Mexican breakfast: rolls toasted, spread with beans and cheese, and baked until melted, then topped with salsa. They go in and out of the oven twice, so you'll practice mitts on, the rack pulled out, and the hot pan set down safely.

why.title: Set the rack before the oven heats
why.body: Racks are easy to move when the oven is cold. Once it's hot, moving one means reaching into a 400°F box. Set it first, in the middle.

why.title: Dry mitts, both hands
why.body: Heat travels through a wet mitt or towel in a second, as steam. Use dry oven mitts on both hands every time you touch the pan, the rack, or the oven door.

why.title: Pull the rack, not the pan
why.body: Reaching into the oven puts your arms near the hot walls. Pull the rack out partway with a mitt, then lift the pan off it, straight up and toward you.

why.title: Toast the bread first
why.body: A quick bake before the toppings go on dries the cut side of the roll, so the beans don't make it soggy.

why.title: A hot pan stays hot
why.body: A sheet pan out of the oven is still hot enough to burn for several minutes. Set it on the stovetop, keep the mitts on, and tell anyone nearby.

wrong.fix: Put the pan back in for 2 more minutes, mitts on.
Toast it longer the first time, until the edges are golden.
Check a few minutes early next time. Ovens run hot or cold.

wrong.sign: The beans are too thick to spread
wrong.fix: Stir in a spoonful of water until they spread easily.

quiz.q: When do you set the oven rack?
quiz.explain: A cold rack is easy and safe to move.

quiz.q: Why must oven mitts be dry?
choices: Heat goes through wet cloth as steam
quiz.explain: A wet mitt burns in a second.

quiz.q: How do you take the pan out?
choices: Pull the rack out partway, then lift the pan
quiz.explain: Your arms stay away from the hot walls.

quiz.q: Where does the hot pan go?

steps.text: Move an oven rack to the middle while the oven is cold. Then heat the oven to 400°F.
steps.tip: The oven takes about 10 minutes to heat. Get everything else ready while you wait.

steps.text: Take the butter out of the fridge so it softens.
Lay a roll flat on the board. Press your hand flat on top and cut it open sideways with the bread knife.
steps.tip: Fingers flat and pointing up, above the blade.

steps.text: Spread a thin layer of butter on the cut sides with the table knife. Lay them cut side up on the sheet pan.
steps.look: 8 halves, buttered side up, not touching.

steps.text: Open the beans and spoon them into the small bowl. Stir them until smooth.
steps.tip: If they're too thick to spread, stir in a spoonful of water.

steps.text: Put dry oven mitts on both hands.
steps.tip: Check that they aren't damp. Wet mitts let heat through.

steps.text: Open the oven door, slide the pan onto the middle of the rack, and close the door.
Mitts on. Pull the rack out partway, lift the pan straight up, and set it on the stovetop.
steps.tip: Push the rack back in and close the door before you do anything else.

steps.text: Spread beans over each half with the spoon. Sprinkle the cheese on top.
steps.tip: Don't touch the pan. Work from above the rolls.

steps.text: Mitts on. Slide the pan back into the oven and bake until the cheese melts.
steps.look: Cheese melted and bubbling at the edges.

steps.text: Mitts on. Pull the rack out, lift out the pan, and set it on the stovetop. Turn off the oven.
steps.tip: Tell anyone nearby that the pan is hot.

steps.text: Let them cool for 2 minutes. Top each with a spoonful of salsa and a few cilantro leaves.
steps.look: Melted cheese, bright salsa on top.
